coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: 20–25 minutes easy, Z2 only (120–130 bpm based on your recent easy runs). This is a shakeout to keep legs loose and flush out yesterday's 3-miler; your recovery score is solid at 71, so you're cleared for gentle movement. Stay flat, no hills, no tempo. You're 24 hours from 2,500m of vert in the Julian Alps—preserve neuromuscular freshness, don't burn glycogen. Think of this as a systems check: confirm your watch is charged, test your race nutrition one more time if you haven't, and dial in your pacing feel for tomorrow's climb.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Today is load day. Eat 7–9g carbs per kg bodyweight (estimate ~500–650g total if you're ~75kg), split across breakfast, lunch, snack, and dinner—prioritize easy-to-digest carbs (rice, pasta, potatoes, fruit, sports drinks). You slept 11.5h with 85% efficiency, which is excellent recovery, but that also means your glycogen depletion was real last week; replenish fully today. Tomorrow you'll start at dawn in cold alpine air on a brutal climb—arrive with full tanks. Protein at each meal (25–30g), minimal fiber and fat to avoid GI friction.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Target 8–9 hours tonight; your resting HR is 68 (4 bpm above 30-day avg), a mild signal your nervous system is still engaged post-taper. No alcohol, no caffeine after 2pm. Elevate legs for 10–15 minutes post-shakeout run. Your recovery score of 71 is green, but sleep quality tonight matters more than quantity—cool, dark, quiet room, no work email after 21:00. You've built the fitness over 34 weeks; these final 24 hours are about showing up rested and ready, not training.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Visualize the first 3km climb out of Kranjska Gora—you'll be at moderate effort (Z3/Z4), working but controlled, aligned with your recent race-pace runs at 129–132 bpm. Sparse aid stations mean you own your pacing; lean on your ultra experience to settle into rhythm early rather than chase others. Tomorrow's course is about sustained climbing and alpine exposure, not speed. You've run 34 weeks for this single day—trust your fitness, execute your fueling plan, and let your executive discipline (which clearly runs deep in your profile) translate to controlled aggression on the mountain.
